x: Youths' Championship, held at Guildford on Jan 14th Belgrave finished a disappointing 6th. Although Hampshire (7th) and Fairclough (14th) ran well, the rest of the team were well below form.
Cyril Forey (a great prospect) was a comfortable winner of the Junior race with John Thresher third; and our Youth success was due to Hampshire and Fairclough being 2nd and 3rd.

Heck, Miller, Thresher, Moore and Johnston are but a few knocking on the door to 1st team honours. There are also those up-and-coming lads Cocks, Hampshire and Fairclough who will be dis-placing a few old-timers before long.

O'Hara and Maclean finished first and second in the mile with two youngsters Fairclough and Bicourt fighting it out for fourth and fifth places to clock 4:31.0 and 4:32.0 respectively.

TOP: Bicourt leads Fairclough, Cocks and Morrison at the half-way mark in the Junior 5 miles Championship for the "Savage" shield. CENTRE LEFT: Linstead, the holder, leads Newell and Black in the Club 10 miles Championship for the "Macher" shield.

Fairclough heads the Juniors---Bicourt the Youths------Hayes the Boys. This is the position at the present time, but who knows how long it will last when we have so many other youngsters striving to depose them?

The only event for Seniors alone was the 2 miles where Bill Kerr lead from gun to tape in 9:10.2, ahead of Dabbs and Fairclough. Chris Ryan scored a junior sprint double over Turnverein's Rotharmel (10.3 and 23.5) but only managed it by a whisker in the 220 yards.
However, despite the absence of Thresher, (defending his London County mile title) and Black and Fairclough (on holiday) we still finished a respectable 4th.

Our first eight, Gerry North, Thresher, Fairclough, Geoff. North, O'Hara, Dabbs, Thorpe and Black were to be joined by Hugh Barrow for the "National" at Sheffield, leaving runners of the class of Steer, Reilly and Hart as reserves.

The first of his pupils included Fairclough, Steer and Cocks, who have since proved their worth in the Senior ranks. Tom's coaching school is still going strong at Battersea Park,where he appears each Tuesday to give them their week's programme.
The following week saw three of our Woking performers (Dance, Steer and Black) joined by Thresher, Bicourt and Fairclough to form a strong sextet against tough opposition in the Blackheath Relay.

The team that eventually took part was but a shadow of our full strength with names such as Fairclough, Hart, O'Hara, Steer, Thresher and Whewell missing from the line up.

These two, plus Hart and Fairclough, were missing this time so Whewell and O'Hara were favourites to gain the place medals. After the first lap the expected medallists still had the close company of Dabbs, Major and Bicourt with O'Hara towing them along at a snappy pace.
Well, Whewell and Fairclough at their best are both capable of finishing in the thirties or forties, and that alone would have given us a win.

At the time of writing Fairclough and Major seem to be humming along and Mann is just the runner to give them all a great start. For the short legs Hart, O'Connor, Dance and Diprose look well placed, with the last two places to be scrambled for by Bicourt, O'Hara, Piotrowski, Cross and Kerr.
An injured and frustrated Fairclough was obliged to be a spectator but even he at his best would not have saved the day. Everyone hoped that our runners had got rid of their bad runs all in one day.
Last year we had lost the title, but this year, although without the services of Fairclough and Dance (both injured), we thought, ran and won like a real team for the first time.

With the "National" won - Fairclough 273; Major 302; and Bicourt 392 will complete the first team for the "Nine Cup". Ted Stimpson comments, "If they only trained from the Hall, they would have had six in six".

It coincides with the running into form, just at the right time, of Kerr, Thresher, North, Major and Fairclough. With Bicourt and Hart already in fine fettle we could well be having a celebration dip in the Lido on September 12th.
